text: The gauge condition ∂^μ h̄_μν = 0 that this book uses to reduce the linearized field equations to a wave equation is called the ___ gauge.
explanation: The book calls ∂^μ h̄_μν = 0 the Lorenz gauge, the general-relativistic analog of the electromagnetic Lorenz gauge ∂^μ A_μ = 0. In this gauge the linearized Einstein equations become □h̄_μν = −16πG T_μν/c⁴. (The spelling is Lorenz, after Ludvig Lorenz — distinct from the transverse-traceless gauge fixed afterward.)
